content.title: Why Is Christianity True? Christian Evidences (1905)
content.author: E. Y. Mullins · Christian Culture Press, Chicago
content.note: A Southern Baptist seminary president's book of Christian evidences: the person of Christ, the resurrection, miracles and Christian experience. For a Baptist voice in the classic apologetic arguments. Public domain: may be quoted, with the translator or edition named and an exact locator.
content.read: Downloaded 2026-11-27 to sources/archive-org/ (checksum in Website/SOURCES.md, 'Apologetics fields: the Baptist footing'). Not yet read for any article. 2026-11-27 (plan APOLOGETICS-FIELDS step 6): Chapter XIII, 'The Resurrection of Jesus', sections 188-207 (pp. 188-203), read in full in the held 1905 edition for resurrection-case and easter-alternatives (section 199 reports Strauss's rebuttal of the swoon theory, from Strauss's 1864 popular Life). Cited, not quoted. 2026-11-27 (plan APOLOGETICS-FIELDS step 6, reading-craig-ehrman): Chapter XII sections 170-176 (miracle, science and philosophy, Hume) and chapter XIII sections 188-190 and 206-207 (the resurrection as a hypothesis tested by historical evidence) read in the held 1905 edition for reading-craig-ehrman. Cited, not quoted. 2026-11-27 (plan APOLOGETICS-FIELDS step 7): ch. VII §103 (pp. 97–98) and §113 (pp. 108–110), ch. VIII §121 (pp. 117–118) and ch. IX §136 (p. 134) read in the held 1905 edition for jesus-claims, trilemma and quests-timeline (one sentence of §113 and phrases of §§121, 136 quoted); §§133–135 (pp. 130–133) for jesus and mythicism. 2026-11-27 (plan APOLOGETICS-FIELDS step 8, God & reality): ch. I §22 (the cumulative argument), ch. V §§74, 80–84 (evolution, theistic evolution as a hypothesis, 'The Christian can await with composure...') and ch. VI §§89–99 (pp. 76–90: proof not mathematical, 'All roads lead to God', the arguments from will, mind, design and conscience, the summary 'All that has been evolved was involved') read in the held 1905 edition for the God & reality articles, above all arguments-map, moral-argument, fine-tuning, creation-views and apologetic-methods; short passages quoted.
